status: PASS finite original-role CUDA GLM Flash and Pro K2 state journeys

reader.contract: No K1 prohibition. eagle_worker_v2:756..848 iterates NextN, increases positions and carries each actual hidden to the next forward. IndexTopKShareState keeps same-iteration selection/carry until iteration exit. One trained NextN layer does not limit proposals to one.

implementation: Existing family consumers accept finite maximum_drafts=1 or2. Default K1 is retained. Flash Quark/MLX/GGUF thin wrappers forward the same option; Pro uses its existing Official/Converted Runtime template. This is component functionality, not a new whole-model GLM application.

Second proposal is sampled from real recursive same-epoch NextN logits after consuming actual first proposal. Original target tails consume current/q0/q1 privately. Three actual final-normalized taps are projected together in one T3 original shared-head graph; actual T3 logits pass the established original-weight value reference.

GLM fragment adapter calls the existing hyle::inference::sampling::speculative_prefix. No p/q/logit mutation, host ID reconstruction or replacement greedy selection. Actual q0/q1 distributions, proposals, residual/bonus and valid flags are bound by their real result leases.

Prefix0 means after mandatory current, never pre-current base. Prefix1/2 replay accepted q0/q1 NextN from true target taps and preserve actual corresponding target states. Current+accepted nonterminal drafts is the committed consumed-row count. Same-epoch frozen index selections are unchanged during draft/verify/repair.

Accepted journal slot0/1 is caught up sequentially only after expected-base publication seals the iteration. lag2 becomes1 then0 with original epoch provenance; only then fresh epoch8 consumes the actual residual/bonus. Unverified approximate second/third states are never published as repaired accepted state.

Natural schedule is proposal0/proposal1/accept2/accept3/final4, atomic cursor+5. Independent bounded controlled accept addresses are searched using original distributions and KAT-qualified Philox/F64, are distinct, final=max+1 and commit maxused+1. They prove reachable branch state behavior, not natural acceptance rate.

Caller admits m2/T3 only for quota/context>=3 and non-EOS first proposal. Context/quota2 or first-proposal EOS uses existing m1/T2 three-draw path; context/quota1 is existing target-only p0 one draw with mandatory-current NextN maintenance. Public limits/acceptance mathematics and prior K1 tail proof are reused. No fixed five-draw claim for shorter episodes.

Independent Heads reuse already retired authentic T3 state/ID leases to select quota1/2/3 and second-proposal EOS. Accepted terminal/unemitted proposals remain pending in q0/q1 lease and are not consumed. Cancellation after staged pending+cursor and wrong-type replacement, stale expected-base rejection and same-decision retry leave old Head/RNG intact.

limitations: Finite original tail-layer/NextN components use explicit generated upstream activations/residual token adapter, initial histories and Pro upstream index fixture. This is not complete GLM generation, task quality, throughput, physical-memory peak, all publishers or all backends.

Actual executions are one Flash and one Pro CUDA source journey. Shared paths are instantiated by both CPU/CUDA compile gates; CPU K2 was not additionally run. Selected quantized wrappers expose the option and compile, not every quantized K2 bank rerun.

Natural two-proposal episodes both rejected first proposal. Accepted prefix1/2 and bonus continuations use explicit legal controlled RNG addresses and unmodified real distributions, separately labelled in raw logs.
K2 is the finite component capacity of this patch; it does not introduce an unbounded speculation tree. Existing complete Qwen K2/K4 and generic arbitrary-prefix mathematics are separate evidence.

Final syntax wrapper initially reused an already-created scratch output directory and did not invoke the compiler; corrected separate compile output then passed. Model runs and source images were never overwritten.
